about: Every picture a page under docs/ or README.md shows: the program that drew it, the command line and environment that make it, and the build it was last taken from. tools/pictures/README.md says how to read and use this; tools/pictures/take_pictures.py takes the entries that have "args", and tools/checks/check_doc_pictures.py holds this file to the pages.

hidden-desktop.what: A real window on Windows, drawn by Qt's Windows platform plugin on a second desktop nobody sees (tools/pictures/hidden_desktop.py), not by the offscreen plugin, which draws a missing-glyph box for a drop-down arrow. darkmode=0 is the light theme whatever the desktop is set to; gray keeps coloured subpixel edges out of the text; QT_QPA_FONTDIR is for the offscreen plugin and is taken out.

hidden-desktop-living-room.what: The same, for Hearth, whose Settings and Network pages say the computer's name: the three _CLUSTER_NETWORK_ variables make that name living-room for the run.

There is no singer and nothing is played: the example's own lead vocal is the microphone, sung along to the song as it is heard, and the song goes to an output that plays to nothing, which the window calls "Speakers" (no microphone is opened, no sound device is used). The picture is taken as the song reaches --seek, with the performance going on, so the marks and the ribbon are what they are a moment either side of it. The Karaoke page behind the window names its takes folder, which is under the account's own documents unless it is set: --setting gives it a folder that is nobody's.

This file is one of those renders, copied under this name. Needs an Android device or emulator.
